lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' season has reached the point where excuses start sounding like surrender. Thursday's 5-2 loss to Minnesota extended Toronto's skid to four games, leaving the club 8-11, 12th in the Eastern Conference, 10 games behind, with 18 points. This is not a slump to admire from a distance; it is a team leaking authority. Chris Tanev's absence has become the sharpest symbol. His planned maintenance may preserve him for the long haul, but sitting a stabilizing defender while the losses pile up is a wager Toronto can no longer make casually. The Rogers Centre routine shake-up only underscores the need for something sturdier than theatre. Mike Babcock's return adds spice, not substance. Tonight's 7 p.m. meeting with Edmonton is the test: Tanev is expected back, and Toronto must prove its defence can finally hold.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' offseason has barely begun, and already the club is wrestling with a problem no lineup construction can solve. Anthony Santander's apology for anti-Muslim social-media posts was necessary, but it does not erase the damage; Toronto now has to decide what accountability looks like while protecting a clubhouse and a city built on inclusion. The baseball work remains just as urgent. With the season over and a final points total of -2.0, Ross Atkins must add impact rather than window dressing, particularly in a Japanese free-agent market where Toronto is suddenly viewed as a serious destination. Santander, 32, is the immediate human story, but the roster is the larger one: too much depends on old answers and not enough on fresh ones. Watch the winter meetings for a meaningful Japanese signing or trade - and whether the organization pairs ambition with unmistakable standards before camp opens March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors' slide has become less a slump than an examination of what remains when the stars are stripped away. Thursday's 123-112 loss to Philadelphia made it three straight defeats, following a 98-93 setback against Boston, and left Toronto 5-7, fourth in the Atlantic and five games behind. The hard truth is sitting in the injury report: Kawhi Leonard is out with a knee problem, while Scottie Barnes remains day-to-day with an adductor issue. Toronto has already used seven starting lineups in 12 games. That is not continuity; it is improvisation under fire. RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley improved against the 76ers, but without the club's two premier forwards, improvement has not become victories. The next test is immediate and unforgiving - the Knicks visit Sunday at 6 p.m. ET, with Toronto needing health, resistance and an end to this three-game skid.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season keeps slipping toward the edge, but Washington keeps grabbing it by the collar. The Commanders rallied past the Giants 24-21 on Thursday night, a win that moved them to 3-5-1, kept them third in the NFC East and cut the deficit to two games. Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for the decisive late touchdown, while Luke McCaffrey supplied the night's bit of football ingenuity - stepping out of bounds before touching a kickoff to give Washington possession at the 40. That is the sort of sharp, opportunistic play a 3-5-1 team needs, especially after the recent loss to Los Angeles. It is also not a cure-all: Washington remains inconsistent, and its margin for error is thin. Next comes the test of whether this one-game winning streak becomes a push up the division or merely another reprieve.

article.title: Maple Leafs Host Oilers in Toronto
paragraphs: The Leafs face the Oilers at 7:00 PM tonight on Sportsnet, with projected goaltenders Sergei Bobrovsky and Devon Levi. Toronto enters at 8-11 and 12th in the Eastern Conference, while Morgan Rielly is day-to-day with a lower-body issue. The Leafs have also shaken up their routine at Rogers Centre before another demanding test.

The Blue Jays are already looking toward March, opening their regular season at the Yankees on Thursday, March 25, at 1:35 PM ET. Anthony Santander apologized for anti-Muslim posts, a difficult off-field story for a club preparing for the next season. The Raptors host the Knicks Sunday at 6:00 PM ET, carrying a 5-7 record and fourth place in the Atlantic Division. Washington's Commanders, 3-5-1 and third in the NFC East, next host the Bengals on Monday, November 23. That game follows coverage of Luke McCaffrey's use of an out-of-bounds rule to help Washington win.
